newsitem.title: UK: Virgin Radio deal referred to UK watchdog.
newsitem.headline: Virgin Radio deal referred to UK watchdog.

text.p: The British government on Thursday referred Capital Radio Plc's planned 64.7 million pound ($105.7 million) acquisition of Richard Branson's Virgin Radio to regulators, citing competition concerns.

Nigel Griffiths, minister for Competition and Consumer Affairs, said he referred the deal to the Monopolies and Mergers Commission due to worries about competition in London's radio advertising market.
Capital's shares dropped six percent, falling 31 pence to 475 by 1015 GMT to rank among the top percentage losers on the London Stock Exchange.

Earlier this month, Britain's Radio Authority said it saw no reason to block the deal, which would give Capital a total of three licences in London -- Capital FM, Capital Gold (AM) and Virgin FM -- in addition to one national AM licence.
However, the Radio Authority said it would make no final decision until Britain's Board of Trade had completed its review of the deal.
The MMC was due to make its report by November 14.
